content.title: What is a Subarray?
content.description: A subarray is a contiguous sequence of elements taken from an array. Unlike subsequences, subarrays must occupy consecutive positions.

content.content: Subarray problems are among the most important topics in Data Structures and Algorithms. Many interview questions involve finding the maximum sum, minimum sum, longest valid segment, or counting subarrays that satisfy certain conditions.

content.title: Important Distinction
content.content: A subarray must be contiguous, whereas a subsequence can skip elements.
For an array containing n elements, the total number of possible subarrays is n × (n + 1) / 2. This formula is frequently asked in coding interviews and aptitude rounds.
The Maximum Subarray Sum problem asks us to find the contiguous subarray having the largest possible sum. This is one of the most famous array problems in technical interviews.

content.title: Interview Favorite
content.content: Maximum Subarray Sum is commonly solved using Kadane's Algorithm.

content.content: Prefix Sum is a powerful optimization technique used to answer subarray sum queries efficiently. Instead of repeatedly calculating sums, we precompute cumulative sums.

content.title: Prefix Sum
content.description: PrefixSum[i] stores the sum of all elements from index 0 to index i.

content.title: Key Benefit
content.content: Subarray sums can be computed in O(1) after building the prefix sum array.
Sliding Window is used when we need to process contiguous segments efficiently. Instead of recalculating every subarray, we adjust the current window by adding and removing elements.

items.question: Maximum Subarray Sum
items.answer: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum.

items.question: Minimum Subarray Sum
items.answer: Find the contiguous subarray with the smallest sum.

items.question: Subarray with Given Sum
items.answer: Determine whether a subarray exists whose sum equals a target value.

items.question: Longest Subarray
items.answer: Find the longest contiguous segment satisfying a condition.

items.question: Count Subarrays
items.answer: Calculate the number of valid subarrays meeting specific criteria.

right_points: Uses Prefix Sum or Sliding Window

content.title: Real-Life Analogy
content.content: Imagine analyzing a week's sales data. Instead of recalculating totals for every period repeatedly, you use previous calculations to quickly determine profits over different date ranges. This is similar to solving subarray problems efficiently.

content.title: Industry Usage
content.content: Subarray techniques are used in financial analytics, signal processing, log analysis, performance monitoring, and recommendation systems.

items.question: What is the most common mistake?
Why do solutions become slow?
items.answer: Because every possible subarray is recalculated repeatedly.

items.question: When should Sliding Window be used?
items.answer: When dealing with contiguous segments and fixed or variable window sizes.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Whenever a problem mentions contiguous elements, immediately consider Subarrays, Prefix Sums, Sliding Window, or Kadane's Algorithm.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Subarrays are contiguous portions of an array.
Kadane's Algorithm finds maximum subarray sum in O(n).
Prefix Sum optimizes range sum calculations.
Sliding Window efficiently processes contiguous segments.
Subarray problems are extremely common in coding interviews.
